text:
ConocoPhillips barely moved today, down just 0.07%, but the stock has climbed 5.34% over the past two weeks amid a surge in global oil prices and fuel supply concerns. The company sits at the center of two major market forces right now: crude oil prices have risen sharply (world oil at $125.44/barrel, up significantly), and refinery capacity worldwide has been damaged by wars in Eastern Europe and the Middle East, tightening fuel markets. Today's flat trading likely reflects that most of this positive backdrop is already priced in after yesterday's 3.4% jump.

The reported Trump-Putin diesel deal announced yesterday may be creating cross-currents for the stock. On one hand, a flood of cheap Russian diesel could ease global fuel prices and reduce the supply-driven demand that's been helping oil companies. On the other hand, U.S. sanctions concerns and the ongoing tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz—which just hit wartime highs—mean that global supply disruptions could persist and keep crude prices elevated, benefiting an integrated producer like ConocoPhillips.
